---
title: "Companion curriculum"
subtitle: "The teaching modules of the housing-audit case"
---

The course is built around one exercise: you reproduce a recorded result, vary the analysis behind it, declare one analysis before you run it, and read your result against those of the class. On this site the exercise is taught on the housing-audit case, a field experiment in which emails signed with names meant to indicate a white, a Black or a Hispanic applicant were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, and the [case study](../cases/housing/index.qmd) tells it in full. A short session or a single day has room for that exercise and little else, so the skills around it are taught in these twelve modules, which run from a first line of R to a reanalysis that you can deposit and register. Each module stands on its own, so you can take the one you need and leave the rest.

Every module is written for this case. The modules that run code compute their numbers from the files of the case in `cases/housing/data/` when the page is built, so that a module can be read as a worked analysis as well as an explanation, and you can check each number against your own output.

Nothing here is required for the short session or for a one-day course, which run in full without any module and with no account to create. Their pages point at some modules as optional preparation, at others as the slower companion of a part of the day, and at the rest as reading for afterwards. The [self-study track](../tracks/self-study/index.qmd) reads the modules in its stages, between the tasks of the case.

The modules fall into the three groups of the Companion menu. The first holds the computational tools with which an analysis is written, the second the data and the public records that let others find an analysis and run it again, and the third the statistical methods with which the case is analysed. Within each group the order is roughly the order of what each module assumes.

## Tools {#sec-tools}

- [Getting started with R](intro-r.qmd) – R from the first line, on the emails of the case: objects and data frames, packages, the pipe and the datawizard verbs, a share and a difference in shares, a first table and a first figure, and a first call to `try_spec()`, then the deposited Stata file, the three dialects of R and naming the estimand.
- [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](ide.qmd) – the IDE from which R is driven, Positron pane by pane with RStudio and VS Code beside it, the browser lab, and six steps through the workspace of the case.
- [Quarto and reproducible documents](quarto.qmd) – what a `.qmd` file holds and what rendering does to it, the header and the chunk options of the exercise report, inline code, cross-references, citations, projects and publishing.

## Data and sharing {#sec-sharing}

- [Social science data sources](data-sources.qmd) – the three routes by which data reach a researcher, a map of the archives, surveys, panels and statistics with the access rule for each, the route of the housing-audit file from the Harvard Dataverse, and citing data.
- [Reproducibility repositories](repositories.qmd) – what a repository has to do, the repositories that researchers use, the package of the study on the Harvard Dataverse, the records that SCORE and Multi100 keep on the paper, registrations and preregistration templates, and depositing a reanalysis of your own.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

- [Audit experiments](experiments.qmd) – audit and correspondence studies of discrimination, random assignment and balance, names as treatments, comparisons among replies, randomisation inference, power, and the ethics of deceiving the people whom an audit studies.
- [Binary outcomes](binary-outcomes.qmd) – a 0/1 outcome and its share, the difference in proportions, the linear probability model with HC2 standard errors, logistic regression, odds ratios against average marginal effects, and why a covariate changes an odds ratio even in an experiment.
- [Bayesian estimation](bayesian.qmd) – the gap of the claim as a posterior distribution from a binomial model in brms, priors chosen with a prior predictive check, a weakly informative prior against a sceptical one, the replication as new data, and type S and type M errors.
- [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](dags.qmd) – what a causal graph commits you to, confounders, mediators and colliders, why comparing greetings among replies conditions on a consequence of the name, the graph of the case and the adjustment sets of its curve, and a graph of your own.
- [Simulation as a method](simulation.qmd) – an audit declared and diagnosed with DeclareDesign, the recovery of a planted gap, what a comparison among replies does when the name changes who replies, and power by simulation.
- [The multiverse and its critics](multiverse.qmd) – where multiverse analysis came from, the purposes that a multiverse can serve, the debate of 2025–26 read against the curve of the case, the decomposition of the curve by its decisions, and robustness against replicability.
- [Meta-analysis](meta-analysis.qmd) – the common scale of Multi100 and the problems of converting the five analyses of the case, why five analyses of one file are not five studies, the original audit and its replication pooled with metafor, and equivalence tests with TOSTER.

## Pages on the AR4DS site {#sec-umbrella}

Two topics that do not change with the case live on the [AR4DS site](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/), the umbrella site of the course, and the modules link to them where they are needed. The [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) installs R, an IDE and the workspace, with the [setup help](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) beside it, and [Git and GitHub for reproducible research](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) puts a reanalysis of your own under version control and shares it on GitHub.
